15 The derivation of the pressure equation ∆p = ρ g∆h uses a number of relationships between
quantities.
Which relationship is not used in the derivation of this equation?
mass
A
density = volume
B
potential energy = mass × acceleration of free fall × height
force
C
pressure = area
D
weight = mass × acceleration of free fall

hints: Notice the target equation $\Delta p = \rho g \Delta h$ contains density $\rho$, $g$ and height $\Delta h$ but no energy term.
Connect the pressure change to the weight of a fluid column of volume $A\Delta h$ pressing on base area $A$.
Check each listed relationship in turn and ask whether $\text{mass} \times g \times \text{height}$ as an energy is needed to get force divided by area.
walkthrough: Picture a vertical column of fluid of cross-sectional area $A$ and height $\Delta h$, so its volume is $V = A\Delta h$.
Use density $\rho = m/V$ rearranged to $m = \rho V = \rho A \Delta h$ to find the mass of this column.
Use weight $W = mg$ to find the force due to the column, giving $W = \rho A \Delta h g$.
Use pressure $p = F/A$ with $F = W$, so $\Delta p = W/A = \rho g \Delta h$, which completes the derivation.
The relation $\text{potential energy} = mgh$ was never required, only mass, weight and force per unit area. This is option B

A.explanation: This is used to get the mass of the fluid column from $m = \rho V$ with $V = A\Delta h$.

B.explanation: Gravitational potential energy $mgh$ is not needed because the derivation uses forces and pressure, not energy.

C.explanation: This is used as $\Delta p = F/A$ where $F$ is the weight of fluid above.

D.explanation: This is used to convert the fluid mass $m$ to its weight $W = mg$ acting on the base.
